methodological_rigor.justification: The core design flaw is that the 'pediatric' class is represented by a single cell line (SF188) versus five adult lines, so the classifier is fundamentally learning SF188-vs-rest rather than pediatric-vs-adult biology — the authors acknowledge this but it undermines the primary claim. No power or sample-size justification is provided, no biological or technical replicates are enumerated beyond 'three distinct points' per cell, and spectra from the single pediatric line necessarily appear in both train and test despite the stated 'no spectra from a given cell' rule (that rule applies at cell, not line, level). Statistical reporting lacks confidence intervals on accuracy/AUC, no bootstrap or permutation testing, no multiplicity correction across the many wavenumber comparisons used to assign Table 1 peaks, and the discordance between 10-fold CV accuracy (~66%) and held-out test accuracy (83.6%) is unexplained and raises concern about leakage via per-cell clustering. Differentiation state (BMP4) is described in methods but not integrated as a covariate in analysis, and no cell-line authentication (STR profiling) is reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an in vitro preclinical study on patient-derived GBM neurosphere cell lines with a machine-learning classifier, mapping to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/preclinical). Clinical relevance is modest: age (pediatric vs adult) is already known at the time of surgery, so an intraoperative pediatric-vs-adult classifier addresses a question that clinicians rarely need answered, and the authors do not demonstrate utility for the more clinically meaningful questions (e.g., H3-K27M status, grade, IDH, tumor vs normal margin). The claimed translational path to 'optical biopsy' and 'pediatric neurosurgery' is speculative given cell suspensions on CaF2 slides are far from in situ tissue, and endpoints are classifier metrics rather than patient-relevant outcomes.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD applies as a predictive-model development study (with ARRIVE-adjacent preclinical considerations). Several TRIPOD items are weak or absent: no sample-size rationale, no reporting of calibration, no uncertainty intervals on performance metrics, no explicit handling of missing data or spectra-exclusion counts, and hyperparameter search space is described but final selection rationale is thin given the CV/test discrepancy. Cell-line provenance is given but passage number, authentication, and mycoplasma testing results are only generically asserted. No data repository, no code repository, and no supplementary analysis scripts are referenced in the remaining text, so independent replication is not feasible from the manuscript alone.

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is empirical and incremental: Raman + ML for glioma classification is well established (refs 11, 17, 22, 27–30, 48, 50 cited by the authors themselves), including prior pediatric-brain-tumor Raman work (refs 28, 29, 30, 62). The specific contribution — comparing one pediatric GBM line (SF188) against five adult neurosphere lines with an MLP — is a narrow permutation of existing methodology rather than a conceptual, methodological, or population advance. The 'first-to-compare pediatric vs adult GBM stem cells by Raman-DL' framing is technically defensible but of limited clinical importance since age is clinically known preoperatively, and the single-pediatric-line design precludes a true population-level claim.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and well structured (Intro → Methods → Results → Discussion → Conclusions), and the abstract is quantitatively grounded with the headline metrics. However, there are multiple typographical and grammatical errors ('challanged', 'metholody', 'metabolsim', 'perfomring', 'to ouf knowledge', 'differences lipid composition', 'modularly tailoring'), and the discussion contains speculative mechanistic links that are repeatedly self-flagged as 'speculative,' producing redundancy. Figure captions are informative but Figure 4 is described only as 'methodology' without quantitative content, and Table 1/2 captions in text are terse. The curious discrepancy between CV accuracy (~66%) and test accuracy (83.6%) is reported without analysis, which is a communication problem beyond writing style.

key_strengths: Clear held-out test split with preprocessing/PCA fit only on training data, limiting one common form of leakage
Transparent self-acknowledgement that the 'pediatric' class is a single cell line (SF188), tempering overclaim
Reasonable spectral acquisition protocol (CaF2 substrate, 532 nm, 20 s integration, fingerprint window) with documented instrument settings
Readable Intro–Methods–Results–Discussion flow and quantitatively grounded abstract
key_concerns: Fundamental design flaw: one pediatric line vs five adult lines means the model learns SF188-vs-rest, not pediatric-vs-adult biology — the central claim is not supported
Unexplained gap between 10-fold CV accuracy (~66%) and held-out test accuracy (83.6%) suggests residual leakage or optimistic test-set composition and is not analyzed
No confidence intervals, bootstrap, permutation testing, calibration, or multiplicity correction for the many peak-level comparisons populating Table 1
Clinical motivation is weak because pediatric vs adult status is known preoperatively; translational framing to 'optical biopsy' is speculative given cell-suspension-on-CaF2 setup
No data or code availability, no cell-line authentication (STR), no biological-replicate structure or cell/passage-level accounting reported
Novelty is incremental relative to prior Raman+ML glioma classifiers already cited by the authors (refs 11, 22, 27, 29, 30)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A technically executed but narrowly scoped preclinical proof-of-concept with a design limitation (single pediatric line) that cannot support the pediatric-vs-adult discrimination claim; appropriate venue is a lower-tier journal and only after major revisions addressing additional pediatric lines, uncertainty quantification, and the CV/test discrepancy.
